one_liners.12_words: Crovia records what AI providers disclose about training data, and the absence of it.
one_liners.25_words: Crovia Trust runs TACET, a public log that turns the absence of an AI training-data disclosure into a signed, Bitcoin-anchored, offline-verifiable proof.
one_liners.tweet: Transparency logs prove presence. TACET proves absence over time: hourly, signed, Bitcoin-anchored evidence that an AI model published no training-data disclosure. Every proof is an unmodified Crovia Seal you can verify offline. croviatrust.com/registry/tacet/

boilerplate.50_words: Crovia Trust is an independent observatory of AI training-data disclosure. Its protocol, TACET, records every hour whether AI models on public registries carry a training-data disclosure, signs what it saw, anchors it in Bitcoin, and issues portable proofs of absence — silence you can verify, without trusting Crovia.
boilerplate.100_words: Crovia Trust is an independent observatory of AI training-data disclosure. Existing transparency logs prove that something happened; Crovia's protocol, TACET, proves that something did not. Every hour it opens an epoch with a public randomness beacon, fetches the model cards of the AI systems under watch, runs a published predicate over the bytes, signs the result and closes the hour with a Bitcoin anchor. A model that never discloses accumulates anchored negative observations — and nothing else. The result is a portable proof, delivered as a Crovia Seal, that anyone can verify offline. Data is CC-BY-4.0; specifications are public domain.
boilerplate.200_words:
Crovia Trust is an independent observatory of AI training-data disclosure, based in Italy. It publishes observation facts, never accusations: what a provider disclosed about a model's training data, when, and — its distinctive product — for how long nothing was disclosed at all.

Its core protocol, TACET (Latin: "it is silent"), is a transparency log whose output is a proof of absence over time. Each hour an epoch is opened with a drand randomness round, the public surfaces of the models under watch are fetched, a published predicate is evaluated over the bytes, every observation is signed, and the epoch head is anchored in Bitcoin through OpenTimestamps. Silence never accrues without an anchored negative observation: downtime and gaps count zero. Proofs are sparse-Merkle non-inclusion paths across a contiguous range of epochs, wrapped in an unmodified Crovia Seal (crovia.seal.v1), Crovia's cryptographic receipt format, so any Seal verifier can check them offline.

PNX, a TACET profile, turns the same machinery inward: it lets a company prove that none of its protected assets left an AI agent's run. TACET and Crovia Seal are documented as IETF Internet-Drafts with public conformance vectors and Apache-2.0 reference code; all observation data is CC-BY-4.0 and every weekly snapshot is archived with a DOI.

names.Crovia: the project; also fine: Crovia Trust (the organization). Never 'CROVIA' in prose, never 'Crovia.ai'.
names.TACET: always upper case; the protocol of verifiable silence. Not 'Tacet', not 'the TACET index'.
names.PNX: Proof of Non-Exfiltration; a TACET profile (crovia.pnx.v1).
names.LACUNA: a TACET level-2 silence proof for a model with anchored negative observations; upper case.
names.Crovia Seal: the receipt format, crovia.seal.v1. 'Seal' alone is fine after first mention.
names.silence: always with observed_to: 'silent for N observed days, to <date>'. Never a wall-clock count.
do_not_say: grades, scores, rankings or letter marks (Crovia retired them in September 2026)
that a model 'hides' or 'refuses' anything: Crovia records absence, not intent
that TACET proves what happened between observations
'certified by Crovia': proofs are verifiable, not certifications

assets.rules: Use the mark on dark backgrounds; keep clear space of one mark-height around it; do not recolor, rotate or add effects.

quotes.text: Transparency logs prove presence. TACET proves absence over time.
Precision is the product. The limits are part of the specification.
